items.title: Section: True-Reality Engagement — the Mountain of Bones from Countless Past Lives

items.zh: 汝依如是勝解作意，應當趣入真實作意。於趣入時應作是念：如我今者勝解所作無量青瘀，廣說乃至無量骨鎖，真實青瘀乃至骨鎖，其量過此不可數知。
items.en: "Relying on this confident-understanding engagement, you should now enter into true-reality engagement. Upon entering, you should reflect thus: 'The boundless instances of discoloration my confident understanding has constructed, and so on up through boundless bone-chains — the true, actual number of instances of discoloration, up through bone-chains, far exceeds even this, beyond all counting.'"

items.zh: 從前際來，於彼彼有、彼彼趣中，輪迴生死。我所曾經命終夭沒所棄尸骸、所起青瘀，廣說乃至所起骨鎖，無量無邊。如是所起，推其前際不可知故。假使有能攝聚如是所棄尸骸，令不壞爛，一切大地亦不容受。於一劫中所棄尸骸，乃至骨鎖，假使有能斂在一處，其聚量等廣大脅山。如從前際，後際亦爾，乃至未能作苦邊際。
items.en: "From beginningless time, transmigrating through birth and death across every mode and every destiny of existence — the corpses I myself have left behind, dying at life's end or dying untimely, and the instances of discoloration, up through bone-chains, that arose from them, are boundless and without limit … Were it possible to gather all these discarded corpses together, unrotted, the entire earth could not contain them. Were it possible to gather into a single heap just the corpses discarded within a single eon alone, up through their bone-chains, that heap's size would equal Mount Vipulapārśva. And as it has been from beginningless time past, so shall it continue into time to come, for as long as the very limit of suffering remains unreached."

items.zh: 如是汝依勝解作意，應當趣入真實作意。

items.title: The Precise Rhythm of Alternating Stillness and Insight

items.zh: 又非修習如是青瘀乃至骨鎖毘鉢舍那應頓觀察。纔應於一尸骸青瘀起勝解已，尋復令心於內寂靜。乃至於此所緣境相喜樂明淨，無諸擾惱，不強勵力。齊爾所時，應於如是尸骸青瘀發起勝解。若纔於此乃至勵力方現在前，爾時於內應修寂靜。如於青瘀，乃至骨鎖，當知亦爾。由此道理，乃至無量，當知亦爾。
items.en: "Nor should this insight into discoloration, up through the bone-chain, be practised all at once. As soon as vivid understanding of a single corpse's discoloration has arisen, the mind should promptly be settled into inward stillness. When this object appears joyfully, clearly, and purely, free of any disturbance, without needing to be forced — for as long as that lasts, continue generating vivid understanding of the corpse's discoloration. But the moment it can only be made to appear through forced effort, you should then cultivate inward stillness. As with discoloration, so too, up through the bone-chain — and by this same principle, so too up to the boundless version."

items.title: Stabilising Vivid Understanding into a Settled Quiet

items.zh: 如是令心內寂靜已，復應發起寂靜勝解。謂從最後無量青瘀，乃至最後無量骨鎖，內略其心，方便除遣，安置眾相不顯現中。不全棄捨有分別相，亦不分別。唯即於此所緣境界安住其心，無相、無分別，寂靜而轉。
items.en: Once the mind has thus been settled into inward stillness, one should further generate the vivid understanding of tranquility itself. That is, from the final, boundless discoloration, up through the final, boundless bone-chain, one gathers the mind inward, skilfully dispelling these many marks so that they no longer appear — without entirely abandoning the discriminated mark, and without further discriminating it. One simply settles the mind on this same object, and it proceeds free of marks, free of discursive thought, in tranquility.

items.zh: 彼瑜伽師復應教授。告言：賢首！汝先所取諸光明相，於奢摩他品加行中，及於毘鉢舍那品加行中，皆應作意，如理思惟。若汝能以光明俱心、照了俱心、明淨俱心、無闇俱心，修奢摩他、毘鉢舍那，如是乃為於奢摩他、毘鉢舍那道修光明想。

items.title: Section: Getting the Object Clear From the Very Start — the Mark of Brightness Applied

items.zh: 若有最初於所緣境多不分明，數習勝解，其相闇昧；由是因緣，後所修習所有勝解亦不分明；雖多串習，而相闇昧。若有最初於所緣境多分分明，數習勝解，其相明了；由是因緣，後所修習轉復分明；雖少串習，而相明了。
items.en: If, at the very outset, the object is largely unclear, then repeated practice of vivid understanding will leave its mark obscure; because of this, all later cultivated understanding will likewise remain unclear — however extensively practised, the mark stays obscure. But if, at the very outset, the object is largely clear, then repeated practice of vivid understanding will leave its mark lucid; because of this, later cultivation becomes ever more lucid still — even with little practice, the mark remains clear.

items.zh: 如是汝由善取如是厭離相故，善取如是欣樂相故，善取如是奢摩他相故，善取如是毘鉢舍那相故，善取如是光明相故。於時時中，內以寂靜；於時時中，由隨相行毘鉢舍那思擇諸法；即於不淨正修加行增上力故，於諸念住漸次趣入。將趣入時，

items.title: Section: Entering the Four Foundations of Mindfulness — the Body Contemplated Within, Without, and Both

items.zh: 汝應先於內身所有三十六物，始從髮毛乃至小便，善取其相。汝應於是自內身中諸不淨物，先當發起不淨勝解。數數發起此勝解已，復令其心於內寂靜。如是名為於內身中修循身觀。依自身內而發起故。次應於外諸不淨物，善取其相。汝當發起青瘀勝解，廣說乃至骨鎖勝解；或狹小勝解、或廣大勝解、或無量勝解。數數發起此勝解已，復令其心於內寂靜。如是名為於外身中修循身觀。依他外身而發起故。後復應於自身內外諸不淨物，善取其相，令心明了。又於他身內外不淨，善取其相，令心明了。於自所愛，汝當發起如是勝解。復於死已，出送塚間；至塚間已，棄之在地；棄在地已，至青瘀位、至膿爛位，廣說乃至至骨鎖位，發起勝解。數數發起此勝解已，復令其心於內寂靜。如是名為於內外身修循身觀。
items.en: "You should first, with respect to the thirty-six substances within your own body, beginning with hair and body-hair through to urine, skilfully grasp their marks … This is called cultivating contemplation of the body with respect to the inner body. Next, with respect to the various impure substances outside, you should skilfully grasp their marks. You should generate vivid understanding of discoloration, and so on at length, up through the bone-chain … This is called cultivating contemplation of the body with respect to the outer body. Afterwards, you should skilfully grasp the marks of the impure substances both within and outside your own body, making the mind clear. And with respect to the impure substances both within and outside another's body, you should likewise skilfully grasp their marks, making the mind clear … This is called cultivating contemplation of the body with respect to both the inner and outer body."

items.zh: 依自他身若內若外而發起故。汝復應於四無色蘊，由聞思增上力分別取相，於其三分發起勝解。一、於奢摩他品，二、於無散亂品，三、於毘鉢舍那品。

blocks.text: From imagined images to reflection on what is actually true, and the precise rhythm of alternating calm and insight. Several short passages are untranslated.

The boundless corpses imagined so far are "confident-understanding engagement" (勝解作意), constructed. Now one enters **true-reality engagement** (真實作意): "From beginningless time, the corpses I myself have left behind, dying at life's end or untimely, are boundless"; their heap "would equal a vast mountain range". Venerable Miào Jìng: like "the great Flank Mountain", a mountain shaped like an asura's flank.

"As soon as vivid understanding of a single corpse's discoloration has arisen, settle the mind into inward stillness. When the object appears joyfully and clearly", go on; "the moment it can only be made to appear through forced effort, cultivate inward stillness".

Then generate "the understanding of tranquility itself": gathering the mind inward, dispelling the many marks, "without entirely abandoning the discriminated mark, and without further discriminating it". Venerable Miào Jìng: neither holding nor letting go.
"If, at the very outset, the object is unclear, all later cultivation will likewise remain unclear." Hence the mark of brightness.
"First, with respect to the thirty-six substances within your own body, from hair to urine, grasp their marks": the inner body. Then external corpses: the outer. Then both together.

quiz.q: "Relying on confident understanding, enter true-reality engagement." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain confident understanding?
options: it isn't originally there — it is added afterwards
quiz.why: "Relying on this confident-understanding engagement, you should now enter into true-reality engagement." Master Cháng Bǎi: the first, confident understanding, is something not originally there — added afterwards.

quiz.q: A single eon's corpses "equal 廣大脅山" — the English says "a vast mountain range." How do the masters read it?
options: Miào Jìng: a mountain's name, like an asura's flank; Cháng Bǎi: an asura's back of the hand, enormous
quiz.why: "That heap's size would equal a vast mountain range." Venerable Miào Jìng: like the great Flank Mountain — a mountain's name, shaped like an asura's flank. Master Cháng Bǎi: it refers to an asura's back of the hand, which is enormous. The English doesn't mark it as a proper name.

quiz.q: "This insight should not be practised all at once." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain it?
options: 頓 means all at once — don't observe that way
quiz.why: "Nor should this insight into discoloration, up through the bone-chain, be practised all at once." Venerable Miào Jìng: 頓 means very quickly; "not" — don't observe that way.

quiz.q: Stilled understanding requires "gathering the mind inward." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain it?
options: in calm, don't discriminate much about the discoloration or bones
quiz.why: "One gathers the mind inward, skilfully dispelling these many marks so that they no longer appear — without entirely abandoning the discriminated mark, and without further discriminating it." Venerable Miào Jìng: gathering inward means, in calm, not discriminating much about the object — discoloration or bones.

quiz.q: "If at the outset the object is largely unclear," what happens, according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: unclear at first, it stays unclear however much one practices — a fault
quiz.why: "If, at the very outset, the object is largely unclear, then repeated practice of vivid understanding will leave its mark obscure." Master Cháng Bǎi: if it's unclear at the start, no matter how far you advance, however much you practise, it stays unclear — that is a fault.

quiz.q: "First grasp the thirty-six substances of the inner body." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain "contemplating the body"?
options: from head to foot and back — the first step of body mindfulness
quiz.why: "You should first, with respect to the thirty-six substances within your own body, beginning with hair through to urine, skilfully grasp their marks." Master Cháng Bǎi: 循 means from head to foot — observing the inner body round from head to foot; this is the first step of body mindfulness.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi define "inner" in "contemplating the inner body"?
options: form held by one's own faculties and the storehouse consciousness
quiz.why: "This is called cultivating contemplation of the body with respect to the inner body." Master Cháng Bǎi: if these impure substances are held by one's own five faculties — form appropriated by the storehouse consciousness — they are called inner.
